chunks: Zayd al-Shahham asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a garment in which there is janābah, and the sky rains on me until it becomes wet upon me, so he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.السَّمَاءُ: the sky, meaning rainfall descending from it
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of janabah referred to in relation to the garment
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm or problem in it

ai.seo_question: Is there any harm in wearing a garment affected by janabah if rain falls on it and wets it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a garment affected by janabah and then soaked by rain while being worn. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in this case, indicating permissibility and the absence of a problem in such contact.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.153 - Zayd al-Shahham asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about a garment that has janabah (ritual impurity due to seminal discharge) and is then rained on, causing it to become wet while he is wearing it.
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
